critique:
the policy prompt for subgoal
  When the goal required three pick-up-and-put-down cycles, a completed release left the hand raised and fully open with more cycles remaining. The policy correctly retained target_anchor=[91, 132] and updated completed_cycles to 1, but selected a different cube far from the anchor. A transient lifted-object report had associated that other cube with the hand, whereas the table-height release location and the final visible cube near the anchor agreed on the target. This is a SUFFICIENCY failure in the target-selection rule, not a missing memory fact or an incorrect memory update. Replace the unqualified instruction to use the release trajectory to disambiguate nearby cubes with an evidence-priority rule: for A, select the current table cube consistent with the unchanged target_anchor and the table-height grasp/release location in the current interval, allowing small placement shifts. When those two cues agree, transient lifted-object labels or airborne centroids referring to a different cube must not override them. Use release motion to resolve ambiguity only when it is consistent with these cues; do not transfer target identity solely because another cube is reported as lifted. Point at the selected cube's current visible table center, not an airborne centroid or raised wrist. For example, an anchor at [91, 132], release near [91, 136], and final table cube at [91, 134] identify that cube rather than one at [128, 127]. Exact reproduction of an unobserved recorded grasp coordinate is unnecessary; the point must select the same object. Keep the existing cycle-count updates and A/B/C transition rules.
